_meta.note: Clothing insulation, ensemble summation, required-insulation-in-cold methods, comfort (PMV/PPD) and wind-chill/frostbite figures. Every figure carries its source. confirmed=true means the value was read in the publisher's own document or a verbatim reproduction of it (text extracted from the PDF and read directly); confirmed=false means it came only from a search summary. No value here is an estimate made for this file. Units: 1 clo = 0.155 m2.K/W and 1 met = 58.2 W/m2 (ISO 7730:2005, Clause 4.1 NOTE, confirmed).

ashraeSimpleSum.wording: The insulation of the ensemble is estimated as the sum of the individual values listed in Table 5.2.2.2B.
ashraeSimpleSum.workedExample: overalls + flannel shirt + T-shirt + briefs + boots + calf-length socks: Icl = 0.30 + 0.34 + 0.08 + 0.04 + 0.10 + 0.03 = 0.89 clo
ashraeSimpleSum.addSubtractExample: long underwear bottoms added to Ensemble 5: Icl = 1.01 + 0.15 = 1.16 clo

iso9920Regression.origin: Summation equation given in ISO 9920:2009; database originates from McCullough EA, Jones BW, Huck J (1985), ASHRAE Trans 91, 29-47
iso9920Regression.validation: On 14 measured ensembles (0.53 to 3.19 clo measured) the regression equation differed from measurement by -0.17 to +0.18 clo (mean 0.02 clo, RMSD 0.12 clo); the simple sum differed by -0.61 to +0.11 clo (RMSD 0.27 clo). Authors: the simple sum 'works reasonably well' up to about 2 clo.

seatedAdjustment.table: Table 5.2.2.2C Typical Added Insulation when Sitting on a Chair (valid for ensembles with standing insulation 0.5 clo < Icl < 1.2 clo)

activityAdjustment.formula: Icl,active = Icl x (0.6 + 0.4 / M), for 1.2 met < M < 2.0 met (M in met); no adjustment at or below 1.2 met

limitsOfASHRAE55.wording: This standard does not apply to occupants whose clothing insulation exceeds 1.5 clo ... highly impermeable to moisture transport (e.g., chemical protective clothing or rain gear) ... sleeping, reclining in contact with bedding

indoorComfortZone_ASHRAE55.wording: Two zones are shown - one for 0.5 clo of clothing insulation and one for 1.0 clo of insulation. These insulation levels are typical of clothing worn when the outdoor environment is warm and cool, respectively. Comfort zones for intermediate values of clothing insulation are determined by linear interpolation between the limits for 0.5 and 1.0 clo.
indoorComfortZone_ASHRAE55.activity: graphic comfort zone applies to a lightly clothed person engaged in near-sedentary physical activity (metabolic rates between 1.0 and 1.3 met)

comfortZoneOperativeTemperatures_ASHRAE5.interpolation: tmax,Icl = [(Icl - 0.5 clo) tmax,1.0clo + (1.0 clo - Icl) tmax,0.5clo] / 0.5 clo (and likewise tmin)
comfortZoneOperativeTemperatures_ASHRAE5.source: web search summary of ASHRAE 55 (ICC sample pages https://shop.iccsafe.org/media/wysiwyg/material/8950P219-sample.pdf and https://www.lorisweb.com/CMGT235/DIS06/ASHRAE-55-2010.pdf); the PDF text could not be extracted here

operativeTemperaturePerClo_ASHRAE55.wording: For near-sedentary activities where the metabolic rate is approximately 1.2 met, the effect of changing clothing insulation on the optimum operative temperature is approximately 6 C (11 F) per clo.
operativeTemperaturePerClo_ASHRAE55.unit: degC per clo (11 degF per clo)
operativeTemperaturePerClo_ASHRAE55.example: adding a thin long-sleeve sweater (+0.25 clo) lowers the optimum operative temperature by about 6 C/clo x 0.25 clo = 1.5 C (2.8 F)

comfortTemperatureShiftPerTenthClo_ASHRA.wording: The outer comfort zone boundaries shift toward the left or right, depending on clo and met level. An increase of 0.1 clo or 0.1 met corresponds approximately to a 0.8 C (1.4 F) or 0.5 C (0.9 F) reduction in operative temperature to; a decrease of 0.1 clo or 0.1 met corresponds approximately to a 0.8 C (1.4 F) or 0.5 C (0.9 F) increase in operative temperature.

coldIREQ_ISO11079.definition: IREQ: required clothing insulation for the preservation of body heat balance at defined levels of physiological strain (ISO 11079:2007, 3.1.3). IREQ is the resultant clothing insulation required in the actual environmental conditions to maintain the body in a state of thermal equilibrium at acceptable levels of body and skin temperatures (5.2).
coldIREQ_ISO11079.heatBalance: M - W = Eres + Cres + E + K + R + C + S  (ISO 11079 Eq. 1)

equations.IREQ: IREQ = (tsk - tcl) / (R + C)   (Eq. 8), solved for tcl: tcl = tsk - IREQ * (M - W - Eres - Cres - E)  (Eq. 9)
equations.E: E = (psk - pa) / Re,T  (Eq. 4); in the published code E = w * (psk,s - pa) / Re,T with Re,T = (0.06/im) * (Ia,r/fcl + IREQ)
equations.walkingSpeed: vw = 0.0052 * (M - 58.2) (text; code uses M - 58), capped at 0.7 m/s in the published code
equations.resultantClothing: Icl,r = IT,r - Ia,r/fcl; IT,r = IT * (0.54*exp(0.075*ln(ap) - 0.15*va - 0.22*vw) - 0.06*ln(ap) + 0.5); IT = Icl + Ia/fcl; Ia = 0.085 m2.K/W; ap = air permeability of outer fabric, L/(s.m2)

coldIREQ_ISO11079.interpretation: Icl,r < IREQmin: clothing insufficient, limit duration of exposure. IREQmin <= Icl,r <= IREQneutral: clothing sufficient to prevent cooling, 'slightly cool to neutral' sensation. Icl,r > IREQneutral: clothing sufficient, possible risk of overheating at high activity (ISO 11079 Figure 1). If worn insulation is less than required, a duration-limited exposure Dlim = -Qlim / S is calculated.
coldIREQ_ISO11079.activityInput: M in W/m2, evaluated per ISO 8996 (1 met = 58.2 W/m2)
coldIREQ_ISO11079.publishedCode: Full MATLAB functions IREQ_neu and IREQ_min (iterative solution) are printed in Appendix B of d'Ambrosio Alfano et al. 2025.
sources: dambrosio_2025 (Table 1 criteria, Eqs 7-12, Appendix A-B equations and code)
coldIREQ_ISO11079.note: No published table of IREQ by temperature and activity was read; values for any temperature/activity are computed from the method above.

comfortAndUnderdressing_PMV_PPD.units: M, W in W/m2; Icl in m2.K/W; ta, tr, tcl in C; var in m/s; pa in Pa; hc in W/(m2.K)
comfortAndUnderdressing_PMV_PPD.validRange: PMV between -2 and +2; M 46-232 W/m2 (0.8-4 met); Icl 0-0.310 m2.K/W (0-2 clo); ta 10-30 C; tr 10-40 C; var 0-1 m/s; pa 0-2700 Pa
comfortAndUnderdressing_PMV_PPD.voteDistributionBasis: Based on experiments involving 1 300 subjects; percentages of persons predicted to vote

formulaF.value: Wind Chill (F) = 35.74 + 0.6215T - 35.75(V^0.16) + 0.4275T(V^0.16), T = air temperature (F), V = wind speed (mph)
formulaF.validity: Wind chill temperature is only defined for temperatures at or below 50 F and wind speeds above 3 mph.

windChill_NWS.basis: Wind at 33 ft (10 m) corrected to face height; calm assumed 3 mph at the face; if wind is measured at face level multiply by 1.5. Frostbite zones mark wind chills that may produce frostbite on exposed skin in 30 min or less in the most susceptible (95th percentile) of the population, worst case (clear night). 95% of the population experiences frostbite at skin temperature -7.8 C (18 F); about 1-2% at -1 C (30.2 F); 5% at -4.8 C (23.4 F).

frostbiteTimeEquation.units: Ft minutes; Tair F (or C); V10 wind at 33 ft / 10 m in mph (or km/h)
frostbiteTimeEquation.validity: only valid when frostbite time <= 30 min and wind > 16 mph (25 km/h) and <= 50 mph (80.5 km/h)
frostbiteTimeEquation.note: Frostbite will not actually occur when air temperature is above freezing; it takes more than two hours from freezing down to 10 F even with winds up to 50 mph.

frostbiteTimesF_Table3_2a.title: Time to occurrence of frostbite (5% risk of frostbite) in minutes or hours (h), English units

frostbiteTimesC_Table3_2b.title: Time to occurrence of frostbite (5% risk of frostbite, most susceptible segment of the population) in minutes, metric units; used by the Meteorological Service of Canada

nwsChartZones.value: NWS chart shades three frostbite-time zones: 30 minutes, 10 minutes, 5 minutes. The zones are colour bands only; their cell boundaries were not readable as text, so they are not transcribed here (the OFCM Table 3.2a above gives the underlying times).
nwsChartZones.example: At a wind chill of -19 F exposed skin can freeze in 30 minutes (NWS safety page)
